shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures closed lower on Thursday as traders waited to see whether China would agree to buy US grain in conjunction with the Washington summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.

children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures closed lower on Thursday as traders waited to see whether China would agree to buy US grain in conjunction with the Washington summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
There were no concrete signs so far that China intended to buy US corn, analysts said

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Wednesday after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng that they had agreed to extend until January 10 an agreement pausing a trade war that saw mutual tariffs top 100%
The US Department of Agriculture said net US corn export sales in the week ended September 17 totaled 838,300 metric tons for shipment in the current marketing year, below trade expectations
Rain was delaying US harvests in the western Corn Belt, analysts said
CBOT December corn (CZ26) ended down 1-1/2 cents at $5.27-1/2 per bushel
